ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Place a square piece of paper in the Cartesian coordinate system as shown in the figure. The side length of the square paper $ABCD$ is $3$, and points $E$ and $F$ are located on $BC$ and $CD$, respectively. Fold $AB$ and $AD$ along $AE$ and $AF$, respectively, so that points $B$ and $D$ exactly overlap at point $G$. It is known that $3BE=BC$. Please directly write the coordinates of points $D$ and $E$, and find the equation of line $EF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Place a square piece of paper in the Cartesian coordinate system as shown in the figure. The side length of the square paper $ABCD$ is $3$, and points $E$ and $F$ are located on $BC$ and $CD$, respectively. Fold $AB$ and $AD$ along $AE$ and $AF$, respectively, so that points $B$ and $D$ exactly overlap at point $G$. It is known that $3BE=BC$. Please directly write the coordinates of points $D$ and $E$, and find the equation of line $EF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} The coordinates of point $D$ are $(3,3)$; the coordinates of point $E$ are $(1,0)$;\\ Let the equation of line $EF$ be $y=kx+b$,\\ therefore $\left\{\begin{array}{l} k+b=0 \\ 3k+b=\frac{3}{2} \end{array}\right.$,\\ thus, $\left\{\begin{array}{l} k=\frac{3}{4} \\ b=-\frac{3}{4} \end{array}\right.$,\\ hence the equation of line $EF$ is $\boxed{y=\frac{3}{4}x-\frac{3}{4}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Place a square piece of paper in the Cartesian coordinate system as shown in the figure. Fold $AB$ and $AD$ along $AE$ and $AF$, respectively, so that points $B$ and $D$ exactly overlap at point $G$. It is known that $3BE=BC$. Please directly write the coordinates of points $D$ and $E$, and find the equation of line $EF$.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} The coordinates of point $D$ are $(3,3)$; the coordinates of point $E$ are $(1,0)$;\\ Let the equation of line $EF$ be $y=kx+b$,\\ therefore $\left\{\begin{array}{l} k+b=0 \\ 3k+b=\frac{3}{2} \end{array}\right.$,\\ thus, $\left\{\begin{array}{l} k=\frac{3}{4} \\ b=-\frac{3}{4} \end{array}\right.$,\\ hence the equation of line $EF$ is $\boxed{y=\frac{3}{4}x-\frac{3}{4}}$;
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The coordinate axes in the figure show that point B is at the origin position, BC is along the positive direction of the x-axis, and AB is along the positive direction of the y-axis; ABCD is a square with side length 3, D is at the upper right corner, E is on BC, F is on CD, the fold lines are AE and AF, and B and D coincide after folding at the interior point G. Reasoning: From the figure, take B=(0,0), A=(0,3), C=(3,0), so D=(3,3). Because 3BE=BC and BC=3, BE=1. E is on the x-axis, so E=(1,0). The fold line AE passes through A(0,3) and E(1,0), and its equation is y=-3x+3, namely 3x+y-3=0. B=(0,0) is reflected about line AE to G; using the point-to-line reflection formula gives G=(9/5,3/5). Let F=(3,t). Because after AD is folded along AF, D also goes to G, AF is the perpendicular bisector of DG, and F is on AF, so FD=FG. Thus (3-t)^2=(3-9/5)^2+(t-3/5)^2. Solving gives t=3/2, so F=(3,3/2). The line EF passes through E(1,0) and F(3,3/2), with slope k=((3/2)-0)/(3-1)=3/4, therefore its equation is y=3/4 x - 3/4.
